name: Eventstream Azure Event Hubs source with workspace identity (no shared keys)
description: Connect an Eventstream to an Azure Event Hubs source using the Fabric WORKSPACE IDENTITY instead of a shared access key / connection string. Access is managed through Azure RBAC (assign the workspace identity the Event Hubs Data Receiver role), so no secret is stored in the connection and Fabric rotates the identity credentials automatically. fabio already supports this end to end via 'connection create --credential-type WorkspaceIdentity' — verified: the EventHub connection type lists WorkspaceIdentity among its supported credential types.
prerequisites: Authenticated via fabio auth login (Fabric) and az login (for the Azure RBAC step)
An existing Eventstream item ($ES) in the workspace ($WS)
An Azure Event Hubs namespace + event hub you own (to assign RBAC on)
Workspace Admin (to provision the workspace identity) and Owner/User Access Administrator on the Event Hubs namespace (to assign the role)

steps.description: Provision the workspace identity (async LRO). Skip if the workspace already has one.
steps.notes: Provisioning is asynchronous — verify completion and read the identity's service principal (applicationId / objectId) with 'fabio workspace show --id $WS' (needed for the RBAC assignment in step 2). Use the global --lro-timeout to bound the wait.

steps.command: az role assignment create --assignee <workspace-identity-objectId> --role "Azure Event Hubs Data Receiver" --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.EventHub/namespaces/<namespace>
steps.description: Grant the workspace identity read access to the Event Hubs namespace via Azure RBAC (outside fabio).
steps.notes: The 'Azure Event Hubs Data Receiver' role is what Eventstream needs to consume events. --assignee is the workspace identity's objectId from step 1. Scope to the namespace (or a specific event hub) as your policy requires.

steps.command: fabio connection create --name "eh-wsid" --connectivity-type ShareableCloud --connection-type EventHub --creation-method EventHub.Contents --parameters '{"endpoint":"sb://<namespace>.servicebus.windows.net","entityPath":"<eventhub-name>"}' --credential-type WorkspaceIdentity
steps.description: Create the Fabric connection using the workspace identity — NO shared key, NO --credentials needed (fabio auto-builds {credentialType: WorkspaceIdentity}).
steps.notes: EventHub connections do NOT support skip-test-connection (supportsSkipTestConnection=false), so creation actually tests reachability — the RBAC assignment in step 2 must be effective first. 'endpoint' is the Event Hubs namespace endpoint (sb://<namespace>.servicebus.windows.net); 'entityPath' is the event hub name. Capture the returned connection id ($CONN).

steps.description: Add the Event Hub as an Eventstream source, referencing the workspace-identity connection by id.
steps.notes: AzureEventHubSourceProperties requires dataConnectionId (the connection from step 3), consumerGroupName ($Default unless you created a dedicated group), and inputSerialization (type Json|Csv|Avro; JSON encoding is UTF8). add-source fetches the current definition, merges, and updates.

steps.description: Verify the source was added and is wired to the connection.
steps.notes: get-topology lists all sources/destinations/operators (find 'eh-source' by name). To inspect one source directly use 'fabio eventstream get-source --workspace $WS --id $ES --source-id <SOURCE_ID>' (the source id from the add-source response). 'resume-source' / 'get-source-connection' confirm it is running.

tips: Identity-based auth removes the shared-key management burden: no connection string stored in the connection, and Fabric manages/rotates the identity credentials — you only manage access via Azure RBAC.
Rotate access by changing the RBAC assignment on the namespace; the connection itself never needs editing.
The same 'connection create --credential-type WorkspaceIdentity' works for other Azure sources whose connection type lists WorkspaceIdentity in 'fabio connection list-supported-types'.

If connection creation fails auth: confirm the workspace identity has the Event Hubs Data Receiver role and that role propagation completed (can take a minute), and that the 'endpoint' matches the namespace exactly.
This replaces the older pattern of a SharedAccessSignature/Basic EventHub connection carrying the SAS key.
